// Part: room: H3 lobby and stair hall (the ironmonger's stair hall: iron and dark wood).
// Inner air x 2..4, z 8..23, clear y 2..7 (world). The stair joiner's flight 1 (x 2..3, z 12..17) and flight 2 (x 4,
// z 15..19) are already built and locked. Lane kept clear: x 3 at z 8 (front door's first cell), x 4 from z 8 to 23
// (flight 2's foot and the keeper's door at x 5 z 22), x 3 at z 23 (rear door's first cell).
// Furniture sits on the west column x 2, against the wall, so the lane stays one cell wide and clear.
// Layers are drawn at world y (floor y 2 for the stock, y 7 for the hanging lanterns under the landing).
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

// x 1..5 across, z 7..24 down; '.' leaves the cell alone
function rowsFrom(sparse) {
  return Array.from({ length: 18 }, (_, i) => sparse[7 + i] ?? ".....");
}

const STOCK = {
  B: "barrel",
  A: ["anvil", { facing: "west" }],
  C: ["chest", { facing: "east" }],
  L: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
};

const LIGHTS = {
  L: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }],
};

export function build(g) {
  // ground layer: the focal anvil by the front door, barrels of stock to the front, a chest and barrels under the landing
  layers(g, [1, 2, 7], STOCK, rowsFrom({
    8: ".B...",
    9: ".A...",
    10: ".B...",
    11: ".L...",
    19: ".C...",
    20: ".B...",
    21: ".B...",
  }));
  // hanging lanterns from the flat floor (y 8) over the front zone and under the landing
  layers(g, [1, 7, 7], LIGHTS, rowsFrom({
    9: "..L..",
    14: "...L.",
    18: ".L.L.",
    20: "..L..",
  }));
}

input.summary:
parts/room-9.mjs (H3 lobby and stair hall) now builds with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks; make.sh produced build.nbt (16029 cells).
Fix: the anvil moved from z 9 to z 10 and the barrel at z 20 moved to z 22, because the lighting part's standing lanterns hold (2,2,9) and (2,2,20).
The barrel that sat at z 10 was dropped to make room for the anvil; the lobby keeps 2 barrels, 1 anvil and 1 chest.

waste.what: Finding which earlier-part cells my writes collided with. I read parts-report.json and lights.mjs by hand to learn that the lighting part puts lanterns at (2,2,9) and (2,2,20).
waste.cost: 2 file reads, plus one full make.sh run to see the refusals, then a second run to confirm.
waste.tool: A preflight, e.g. `mcd plan --claims <part>` or a layers() dry-run, that lists which cells of a part's legend are already owned by earlier parts and by which block, before the part is written.

waste.what: Choosing new cells for the displaced anvil and barrel by hand, and checking they stay out of the stair-flight and lane cells.
waste.cost: Worked out the x 2 column cell by cell from the sparse rows; about 3 edits.
waste.tool: A `layers()` option that takes a list of blocked cells (or a `free:` mask) so a part can place stock into the open cells of a column without hand-checking each one.

waste.what: Checking off-palette blocks by hand against palette.json (the objects list) rather than from the report.
waste.tool: `mcd palette-check <part>` (or the make.sh report) that prints off-palette ids with the nearest palette id, so the swap is a lookup.

left: The dropped barrel at z 10 means the lobby has one less barrel than the first draft; that is a design choice, not a fix to the planned look.

I did not run `mcd walk` or `mcd room` on the H3 lobby, so the lane through x 3 and x 4 is not checked for reachability after the move; the barrel at (2,2,22) sits on the x 2 column and should not block the lane, but that is unverified.
The stair-flight and lobby cells were not re-checked with `$MCD sockets check`; the make.sh build passed without refusals for this part.
